subject: computing
subtitle: Identifying repeating structures to create efficient, reusable solutions.

data.targetWord: identifying similarities, trends, or repeating structures in problems or data, in order to apply the same solution to multiple similar cases

examples.en-GB: Pattern recognition helped the programmer notice that the same score-calculation block appeared three times and replace it with a function.

data.targetWord: an ordered list of values or steps following a rule, such as each number increasing by a fixed amount

examples.en-GB: The sequence 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 has a pattern: each term increases by 2.

data.targetWord: a reusable structure or format that can be applied to multiple similar problems, saving the programmer from designing a new solution each time

examples.en-GB: A login form template is reused on every website page that requires authentication.

data.targetWord: creating a solution broad enough to apply to many similar problems, not just the specific case it was originally written for

examples.en-GB: The calculateArea(length, width) function is a generalisation that works for any rectangle, not just the first one it was tested on.

data.targetWord: repeating a set of instructions a number of times — the programming response to recognising a repetition pattern

examples.en-GB: Iteration using a FOR loop replaces writing the same OUTPUT instruction fifty times.

data.targetWord: a situation where the same block of code or action needs to run multiple times, which a programmer resolves by writing a loop

examples.en-GB: Printing 'Hello' ten times is a repetition pattern — it is resolved with a FOR loop rather than ten separate OUTPUT lines.

data.targetWord: a situation where the same calculation or process appears in multiple different places in a program, which a programmer resolves by writing a function

examples.en-GB: A repeated-task pattern for calculating a rectangle's area three times is resolved by writing one calculateArea() function.

data.targetWord: a branch of artificial intelligence where systems identify patterns in large datasets to make predictions or decisions automatically

examples.en-GB: Machine learning enables a spam filter to recognise patterns in unwanted emails and block them automatically.

data.targetWord: a finite, unambiguous sequence of steps designed to solve a problem, often built around a recognised pattern

examples.en-GB: Once the programmer recognised the sorting pattern, they implemented the bubble sort algorithm to handle it.

data.targetWord: a programming construct that repeats a block of instructions, used when a repetition pattern is identified in a problem

examples.en-GB: A FOR loop iterates through all ten enemies in the game, applying the same draw and update logic to each.

data.targetWord: a named subroutine that performs a specific task and returns a value; the programming response to a repeated-task pattern

examples.en-GB: Writing a calculateAverage(scores) function avoids repeating the same averaging code in three different places.

data.targetWord: a collection of pre-written, reusable code modules that solve common programming patterns so programmers do not have to rewrite them

examples.en-GB: The sorting library provides a ready-made solution to the 'sort a list' pattern, saving every programmer from writing their own version.

data.targetWord: the ability of code, a function, or a module to be applied to multiple similar problems without being rewritten each time

examples.en-GB: The reusability of the validateEmail() function means it is called from the registration page, the login page, and the settings page.

data.targetWord: a pattern visible in a dataset where values change in a consistent, predictable direction over time or across conditions

examples.en-GB: The data trend in the temperature readings showed a rise of 15 degrees every five minutes.

data.targetWord: using a recognised pattern in existing data to calculate or estimate what future data values will be

examples.en-GB: After identifying the temperature trend, the scientist made a prediction that the temperature at 25 minutes would be 95 degrees.

data.targetWord: a shared structure or characteristic between two or more problems or datasets that allows the same solution to be applied to both

examples.en-GB: The similarity between processing a photo and processing a video frame meant the same compression function could be reused.

data.targetWord: a software system that uses pattern recognition to identify characteristics common to unwanted emails and automatically route them to the spam folder

examples.en-GB: The spam filter recognised patterns such as 'FREE!!!' in the subject line and flagged those emails automatically.

data.targetWord: a number sequence where each term is the sum of the two preceding terms: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…; a classic example of a pattern in data

examples.en-GB: Once the Fibonacci pattern is recognised, a loop or recursive function can generate any number of terms efficiently.

data.targetWord: a count-controlled loop that repeats a block of code a fixed number of times; the direct programming response to a repetition pattern

examples.en-GB: A FOR loop from 1 to 10 generates the even-number sequence 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 without writing each output separately.

data.targetWord: a data structure that stores multiple values of the same type under one name, often used when pattern recognition shows that several items share the same structure

examples.en-GB: Storing all ten enemy positions in an array makes it possible to use a loop to process them all with the same code.

data.targetWord: a pre-built collection of code that provides ready-made solutions to common website-building patterns, such as routing and form handling

examples.en-GB: Using a web framework means a programmer does not have to re-implement the login or routing pattern every time they build a website.

data.targetWord: a recurring arrangement or organisation that appears across multiple programs, which can be packaged into a template or library

examples.en-GB: The structural pattern of reading a file, processing its contents, and writing output appears in many programs and can be reused.

data.targetWord: code that achieves the same result with fewer lines, less repetition, and lower chance of introducing bugs by using loops, functions, and libraries

examples.en-GB: Using a loop instead of 100 identical OUTPUT lines produces efficient code that is also easier to maintain.

data.targetWord: a large dataset used to teach a machine learning system to recognise patterns so it can make predictions on new, unseen data

examples.en-GB: The spam filter was trained on thousands of spam examples, allowing it to recognise patterns in new emails.

data.targetWord: a recurring relationship or trend within a dataset, such as a sequence that increases by a fixed amount each step

examples.en-GB: A pattern in data was identified: sales always rose by 20% in December each year.

data.sentence: Identifying similarities, trends, and repeating structures in problems or data is called ____.
In the sequence 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, the pattern is that each number increases by ____.
When the same action needs to repeat a fixed number of times, a programmer uses a ____ to respond to the repetition pattern.
When the same calculation appears in multiple places in a program, a programmer creates a ____ to avoid repeating the code.
A solution that works for many similar problems, not just one specific case, is called a ____.
In the Fibonacci sequence 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, each number is the ____ of the two numbers before it.
A spam filter uses pattern recognition to identify common characteristics of ____ emails and block them automatically.
Collections of pre-written, reusable code solutions to common programming patterns are called ____.
____ learning is a branch of AI where systems identify patterns in large datasets to make predictions.
A game needs to draw 10 enemies. Instead of writing separate code for each, a programmer uses a ____ to process all enemies with the same logic.
If a weather dataset shows temperature rising by 15 degrees every 5 minutes, this ____ in data allows future values to be predicted.
Code that achieves the same result in fewer lines with less repetition is called ____ code.
Storing ten enemies in a single ____ allows a loop to process them all with the same code.
Recognising that the ask-accept-check pattern repeats 10 times in a quiz program allows it to be reduced to a single ____ block.
Pattern recognition directly determines which programming ____ to use: repetition patterns lead to loops; repeated tasks lead to functions.

data.title: Responding to a repeated pattern in code
data.instruction: Put these steps in the correct order for how a programmer handles a repeated pattern.
items: Identify the repeated block of code or process
Abstract the repeated logic into a general solution
Create a function or loop that implements the solution
Replace each repeated instance with a call to the function or loop
Test the new function or loop with different inputs
Reuse the generalised solution wherever the same pattern occurs again

data.title: Pattern in data or pattern in code?
data.instruction: Sort each example into the correct category.

data.instruction: For each programming pattern, decide whether the best response is a FOR loop or a function.

Printing each item in a list of 50 names one by one
